answer: A concrete defense is a harbor registry binding each credential to one reef-scoped quota, released only in proportion to verified outward deliveries recorded by the counterparty, never by the agent itself. A credential holding surplus capacity must park it in an umber escrow for a fixed number of epochs before drawing again, the escrow keyed to the delivering credential, not the wallet behind it. Cloning therefore multiplies parked capital instead of usable throughput, while the release schedule is public, so an observer can price the cost of a fork.
